caption: A scene adapter steps one ProcessWorld from Unity's Update, LateUpdate and FixedUpdate. Register through the builder: ProcessControl.Register(x).HandledBy(h).With(data).In(world).Run(out relay)
Every process implements IGameplayProcess. A Lazy base idles in RunProcess and lives on its step hooks; both GAS hubs, TaskSequenceProcess and GroupProcess derive from one.
An immutable definition with one TaskSequenceRuntime per live run, so runs can overlap. Each registration makes a fresh TaskSequenceProcess.
The default transitions of each EProcessLifecycle.
Which phase each system steps in. A GAS hub steps at UpdateAndLate: GASCore.Tick() in Update, its end of frame in LateUpdate.
IGameplayAbilitySystem is the entity contract. Both hubs implement it and forward to one internal GASCore, which reads only a RuntimeEntityIdentity.
What GASCore keeps besides the subsystems, the ActionQueue its end of frame drains, and the identity's death rules and entity components.
From the Bootstrapper to a registered entity. The runtime hub initializes in its constructor, the Mono hub when it registers.
What triggers death, what each EntityDeath policy does at the end of frame, and how an entity revives.
The asset, its grant as an AbilitySpec in an AbilitySpecContainer slot, and one activation: an AbilityDataPacket and a pooled AbilityProxy that compiles lazily.
What a game derives from: ability tasks, targeting tasks, ability components, validation rules and recharges. Task instances belong to the asset and are shared.
From the request through the checks, targeting, usage, stages and tasks to the end. Each activation is two processes HandledBy the caster, in ProcessWorld.Of(caster).
The first impact entry is derived on every Generate() and never serialized. The Additional Impacts are authored entries, each with its own delivery. A spec's icon can come from its origin.
EffectSystemComponent is the per-entity shelf. Each shelved container is linked both ways to its spec, and the duration's policies decide how a re-application lands.
What an effect carries besides its impacts: components with lifecycle hooks, cues for presentation, modifiers that change other effects, and purges.
From GenerateEffectSpec through the shelf's gates, the commits or the modifiers, the impact relay to the dealer, the ticks and the removal.
Attribute and AttributeSet assets become one CachedAttributeValue per attribute. Every change goes through one of the four verbs.
What one change runs through, from the verb to the end of frame. Register and Unregister keep the transport value; only a Commit previews its delta.
Every authored number is a ScalableFloat or ScalableInt: a magnitude and a scaler, read with a NumberContext. NumberContext.Of has an overload for every place a number is read, ItemSpec included.
How number.Evaluate(NumberContext.Of(x)) reaches a value, from the constant check to the combine.
Each entity's TagCache holds weights, listeners and tag workers. Show a tag with ToString(), its DisplayName, never its raw Name.
Reactive rules in five families. A StandardWorkerGroup routes each family to the cache that runs it; effect workers run per application of the effect that lists them.
An Item asset becomes an ItemSpec in an ItemSpecContainer slot. The spec is the origin of the item's effects, and its level lives under the item's AssetTag.
Given, equipped, used, consumed, unequipped and removed. Uses and Consume are two independent routes to spending an item.

Which asset holds which. Every asset derives from BaseForgeAsset, the levelled ones from BaseForgeLevelProvider. An Ability, effect, Item, AttributeSet or entity can LinkToProvider and follow another's level.
